findings.message: `rollback-diagnoser` は純粋な判断レーンとして `xhigh` を割り当てる設計意図ですが、プロファイルと Claude adapter の双方で `high` になっています。これにより設計で定めた effort 配分と実際の実行設定がずれます。`reasoning_effort` と frontmatter の `effort` をともに `xhigh` に揃えてください。

`dry-fix-lead` を Claude に切り替えると `/track:dry-check` が必ず失敗します。正規 wrapper は `.claude/commands/track/dry-check.md:13` で Codex のみ対応し、Claude 時の Agent fallback も禁止しています。実装も `libs/infrastructure/src/dry_check/dry_fix_local/mod.rs:110` で Codex 以外を `unsupported` として拒否します。Claude dispatch sentinel を実装するまで provider を Codex に戻す必要があります。

`<!-- illustrative, non-canonical -->` が付いた内容を無条件で対象外にすると、任意の長さの schema/code 例が decision を埋没させても報告不能になります。これは冒頭の「concisely」原則と、77行目の「structural bloat is NOT a nit」に矛盾します。marker は例を canonical decision と誤認しないために使いつつ、量によって decision を obscuring する場合は引き続き報告可能にしてください。

`track-local-dry-fix` は dispatch sentinel を出しません。現行実装は Codex を直接実行し、他 provider は fail-closed します。この記述は同ファイル29行目と実装契約に反し、存在しない sentinel を待つ誤った配線を案内します。sentinel の説明を `track-local-review-fix` のみに限定してください。

`adr-editor` は今回 Claude に切り替わり、この明示的 tools list が実行時境界になりますが、`Write` がありません。capability SSoT は Phase 1+ の delta candidate や hearing ADR の新規ファイル作成を `Edit` / `Write` で行う契約です。`Edit` だけでは新規 ADR を作成できないため、これらの必須経路を完遂できません。

書き直された対応表は `impl-planner` の成果物を `impl-plan.json` と `task-coverage.json` の2つだけとしていますが、capability SSoT と CLAUDE.md の Phase 3 契約では `task-contract.json` も必須です。同じ欠落が `impl-planner.md` の description にもあり、Claude dispatch が必須 attribution artifact を省略すると task-contract coverage / pre-review gate が停止します。

Propagate `task-contract.json` through the `/track:impl-plan` workflow contract. This description now correctly declares three owned artifacts, but `.harness/workflows/track/impl-plan.md`, `.claude/commands/track/impl-plan.md`, and `.agents/skills/track-impl-plan/SKILL.md` still define and report only `impl-plan.json` and `task-coverage.json`. The provider adapters and workflow SSoT therefore disagree about Phase 3 outputs and the Codex adapter's write surface omits the third artifact.

Preserve the diagnoser's strict read-only boundary. `.harness/capabilities/adr-diagnoser.md:159-166` forbids editing any repository file, but this live Claude adapter permits writes under `tmp/` by saying only that nothing may be written outside it. Because the adapter exposes Bash, this weakens the provider-independent contract; diff inspection must remain non-writing.

Update the shipped provider documentation with the researcher switch. The active profile now routes `researcher` to Claude, while `README.md:68` still says the default researcher is Gemini; the sample default routes it to Codex, so neither default selects Gemini. Fresh consumers are therefore given a false provider prerequisite inconsistent with the routing SSoT.

The Codex in-host impl-planner path is not wired to the new three-artifact contract. This skill delegates to `.codex/agents/impl-planner.toml`, whose higher-priority instructions still own only `impl-plan.json` and `task-coverage.json` while claiming the capability generates `plan.md`. Under the codex-heavy profile this can omit the required `task-contract.json`, and `plan.md` ownership contradicts the capability SSoT. Update the Codex agent/skill projection and remove the `plan.md` claim.

The new `task-contract.json` output was not propagated to the parent planning surfaces. `.harness/workflows/track/plan.md` still lists only two Phase 3 artifacts in its ownership and output sections, and `.claude/commands/track/plan.md` omits it from the final report. Consequently `/track:plan` and its child workflow now expose inconsistent artifact contracts.

The blanket exemption for every prohibition or fail-closed condition contradicts the preceding removability test and the stated rule that workflow/capability SSoTs own operational detail. A duplicated operational fail-closed rule already recorded in an existing workflow can be removed from an ADR without changing any decision, but this carve-out makes such gate or recovery bloat unreportable. Limit the exemption to cases where the prohibition itself is the recorded decision.

The adapter says `impl-planner` triggers a CLI render of `plan.md`, but the capability SSoT only writes the three JSON artifacts and runs `bin/sotp verify plan-artifact-refs`; it explicitly forbids writing `plan.md` and permits no view-sync command. Remove this unsupported side effect or add it to the provider-agnostic workflow/capability contract.

Switching the root orchestrator to Claude activates `.claude/rules/orchestration.md`, whose Phase 3 model, required-reading list, and impl-planner ownership still name only `impl-plan.json` and `task-coverage.json` (lines 24, 39, and 92), contradicting the newly synchronized three-artifact contract. Update that live Claude rule to include `task-contract.json`.

This batch changes the shared reviewer fast-round reasoning policy solely to compensate for a prior review-loop failure, but the track’s stated document-move scope and acceptance criteria do not own or justify `.harness/config/agent-profiles.json`. This unrelated harness-policy mutation should be reverted here and proposed as a separate change; otherwise the track couples convention ownership with a global reviewer-runtime behavior change.

Changing the reviewer fast effort to `medium` leaves two committed-profile tests hard-coded to `ReasoningEffort::Low`: `test_committed_profiles_subprocess_entries_resolve_explicit_effort` and `test_committed_and_default_profiles_resolve_full_cli_effort_contract` in `libs/infrastructure/src/agent_profiles/tests.rs` (lines 232–234 and 282–285). Because those tests load this file and the default sample directly, the Rust CI now fails. Update or decouple those assertions together with the four profile defaults.

移動後の reference が廃止済みの permission enforcement を現行契約として公開しています。実際の `.claude/settings.json` で明示的に deny されるのは `install` / `chmod` / `chown` のみで、`FORBIDDEN_ALLOW` verifier も現行 source に存在しません。さらに `.claude/rules/guardrails.md` は permission 設定を consumer-owned・CI 非強制と明記しています。このままでは consumer が `touch` / `cp` / `mv` も hard-deny され、CI が allowlist を拒否すると誤認するため、deny 一覧を実設定に合わせ、Layer 3 を CI enforcement ではなく推奨 permission posture として記述してください。

This distributed policy links to `knowledge/adr/README.md`, but `knowledge/adr` is overlay-classified and absent from a fresh exported consumer scaffold. Following this link therefore breaks in consumers; remove the concrete link or point to a distributed reference.

This distributed policy links to `knowledge/adr/README.md`, but `knowledge/adr` is overlay-classified and absent from a fresh exported consumer scaffold. Following this link therefore breaks in consumers; remove the concrete link or point to a distributed reference.

`track/registry.md` は lifecycle policy で `bin/sotp track views sync` が生成する読み取り専用ビューと定義されていますが、この command は欠落時に手作業で最小ファイルを作るよう指示しています。非 canonical な registry を生成し得るため、renderer を実行するか `/track:init` に作成を委ねてください。

registry の再生成契機が実装と一致していません。実際には `/track:init` が初回生成し、各 `bin/sotp track transition` が即座に views sync を実行します。一方、standalone `/track:commit` は状態を変更せず、必要時の sync しか規定していません。表を init・状態遷移・明示的 sync・archive という実際の契機に合わせてください。

この policy はタスク状態遷移を適用外としながら、ここで全タスクを正確に `done` へ遷移してから push する手順を規定しています。canonical merge workflow は merge 時だけ完了を強制し、`done` または `skipped` を完了扱いにして、未完了状態での push／PR review も許可しています。また109行目は workflow SSoT ではなく `/track:merge` の command 本文を所有者として示しています。対応済みタスクを誤って阻止しないよう、この重複手順を除き `.harness/workflows/track/merge.md` を直接参照してください。

git note の `Task` 値を `impl-plan.json`／`plan.md` から取得し、Changes を最大10件とする契約が、canonical commit workflow の「metadata.json の done task または commit subject」かつ件数上限なしという契約と一致していません。`metadata.json` は identity-only なので後者の主要取得元は成立せず、現在は policy と workflow に従う agent が異なる note を生成します。フォーマットの所有者を一つに定め、commit workflow からその文書を直接参照させてください。
例では note の存在理由を「コミット本体から再構築できない情報」の保存と定義していますが、この例外は紛失した note をコミット本体から再構築できると述べており、保持・復旧方針が正反対です。紛失を許容するなら「補助情報なので復旧不要」に留めるなど、再構築可能性の規定を統一してください。

`Task` を `impl-plan.json` の done task から生成するとしていますが、Step 3a は `impl-plan.json` を読まず、batch-first commit で複数 task が done の場合にどれを選ぶか、いつ commit subjectへフォールバックするかも定義していません。このため同じ commit から異なる `Task` 値が生成でき、git-notes policy の「定型部分は引き直せる」という契約も成立しません。`impl-plan.json` を生成入力に追加し、複数 task の列挙または決定的な選択規則を定義してください。

「全コミットは事前レビュー必須」としながら、review workflow は NotStarted bypass を正規の terminal path として扱い、ローカル round なしの PR-based commit を許可しています。PR reviewer は commit 後にしか実行できないため、同じ経路が policy では禁止、workflow では許可になります。PR-based 例外を明記するか、guarded commit では bypass を無効化してください。

bare `git stash` は untracked files を退避しないため、新規ファイルを含む変更では base branch への切替が拒否されるか、base 側テストが dirty state の影響を受けます。復帰・restore 手順もなく、既存障害の判定を信頼できません。隔離された clean checkout または untracked を含む sanctioned な往復手順を定義してください。

Good 例が batch commit 後の hash backfill から直接 PR に進んでいますが、backfill は `impl-plan.json` を再変更するため、full-cycle Step 4 が要求する impl-plan review refresh と lifecycle-tail commit が必要です。merge gate は DonePending を受理するので、この省略は機械的に止まらず、hash を記録しないまま merge できます。tail review/commit を明示してください。

The PR-review lane treats the commit as provisional until the reviewer returns explicit zero findings, but the PR-review workflow also permits a user-approved Accepted Deviations outcome as terminal. Under this policy, that valid workflow outcome remains classified as unjudged indefinitely. Align the terminal conditions with both PR-review outcomes or explicitly prohibit the deviation path.

The policy declares “no unreviewed merge” an invariant while documenting that the NotStarted bypass permits an unreviewed commit and that merge performs no review-approval check. Consequently, commit followed directly by merge can satisfy every mechanical gate without any reviewer verdict. Reliance solely on discipline for this workflow invariant conflicts with the enforce-by-mechanism convention; require a review receipt at merge, remove the bypass, or document a sanctioned exception and reassessment trigger.

Commit-hash backfill is defined as mandatory completion work, but the policy explicitly leaves it to a checklist even though the merge gate accepts DonePending tasks. This makes a normal merge capable of permanently losing required task traceability and leaves an artifact-integrity rule prompt-only, contrary to the enforce-by-mechanism convention. Add enforcement or document a grounded exception and reassessment trigger.

This claims AC fulfillment is mechanically determined from local review.json zero findings and task commit hashes, but the newly documented PR-only lane may legitimately have no review.json, while DonePending tasks without hashes are treated as resolved by both track status and the merge guard. The stated mechanical completion formula therefore does not match any enforced lifecycle. Describe the actual gates or introduce receipts/checks that implement this formula.

`review-protocol.md` declares Accepted Deviations with user approval to be a valid PR-review terminal, but its later unconditional `zero_findings` rule still says the review cycle must continue until the reviewer returns `zero_findings`. Without scoping that rule to the local lane or explicitly exempting the accepted-deviation terminal, the policy contradicts its own PR-review terminal contract.

The policy records measured hash drift (24 of 102 merged tracks, including 7 with all task hashes missing) and says the mechanism reassessment trigger has fired, yet leaves merge permissive and relies only on discipline pending a future ADR. This is an acknowledged operational enforcement gap, not a harmless exception: the current merge path can still close tracks with unrecorded `commit_hash` values, contrary to the lifecycle's stated completion invariant.

運用ドキュメントの対象拡張から provider capability adapters が漏れています。同じ scope の `.claude/agents/adr-diagnoser.md` は `.harness/capabilities/adr-diagnoser.md` の明示的 adapter ですが、禁止対象は `.claude/commands`、`.claude/skills`、`.agents/skills` のみです。このままでは `.claude/agents/**/*.md` や `.codex/agents/*.toml` に日付付き ADR citation が入っても本 policy の適用外になります。Scope と禁止規則の両方へ adapter surface を追加してください。

README は review wrapper が current ADR と最新 baseline の byte match を検証し、baseline 不一致が review を block すると説明しています。しかし移動先 policy と review workflow は、`check-review` が確認するのは init record と ledger-copy integrity のみで、current ADR の divergence は Phase 0 の正常な draft 状態、byte comparison は commit gate と track-aware CI のみと規定しています。review/commit/CI の境界をその契約に合わせて修正してください。

The widened operational-document set still omits actual capability adapters such as `.claude/agents/**/*.md` (including the scoped `adr-diagnoser.md`) and `.codex/agents/*.toml`. Those shipped wrappers can therefore introduce dated ADR citations without violating this policy, preserving the provider-surface coverage gap this change intends to close. Add these surfaces to the scope, rule, and checklist.

This workflow says ADR file existence is the operational approval, but the governing policy explicitly says existence is only a `/track:plan` precondition and does not replace Phase 0 user approval. Clarify that no file-level Status is used while the Phase 0 approval boundary remains mandatory.

`spec.md` is listed as a Source of Truth alongside `spec.json`, contradicting `CLAUDE.md` and the spec-designer contract, which define it as a generated read-only view. This can direct new consumers to edit a derived artifact; list only `spec.json` as the specification SoT.

The README advertises `/track:full-cycle <task>` as single-task execution, but the command adapter accepts no arguments and the workflow consumes a feature batch, splitting only for scope ceilings. This is a user-facing command wiring mismatch; document the no-argument, batch-first invocation.

The README says the review wrapper byte-matches every current recorded ADR against its latest baseline. `check-review` only validates the init designation and stored ledger-copy integrity; working-tree byte comparison is reserved for the commit gate and track-aware CI. The same stale claim also appears earlier at lines 55 and 113, incorrectly presenting normal Phase 0 draft divergence as a review blocker.

This operational capability still cites a specific ADR by bare dated ID (`ADR 2026-07-23-0240 D1`) in its runtime instructions. The policy forbids dated-ADR citations in operational instruction documents, including bare `YYYY-MM-DD-HHMM` forms; replace it with a policy/spec anchor or self-contained wording.

The scope first includes `knowledge/adr/*.md` authoring and updates, then globally excludes “ADR 本体” as historical records. This makes the policy's core ADR lifecycle rules formally inapplicable to the artifacts they govern. Qualify these exclusions as applying only to the dated-ADR citation rule, or move them beneath that rule.

The Codex adapter narrows Step 11 to a “terminal primary-ADR diff-comment,” while the workflow SSoT requires one audit covering every protected source, including later `cite` and adopted `new-adr` sources. Following this adapter can omit required diffs and provenance; update this instruction and the reporting text at line 64 to say all-protected-source terminal audit.

The newly added statement that every SoT is JSON or Markdown contradicts the immediately preceding table, which defines Rust implementation files as the fourth SoT. It also suggests `plan.md` derives from those four SoTs even though it is rendered from `metadata.json`. Describe SoTs as repository files generally and name the actual JSON source for each rendered view.

The Codex adapter still describes Step 11 as a “terminal primary-ADR diff-comment” and repeats that narrowing in its reporting contract at line 64, while the workflow SSoT requires one terminal audit covering every ledger-protected source, including later `cite` and adopted `new-adr` sources. This can cause Codex executions or reports to omit those sources and their provenance; describe the step and result as the all-protected-source terminal audit required by `.harness/workflows/track/adr2pr.md`.

The distributed reference still requires consumers to inspect the sotp source, and the Review Checklist repeats that requirement. Fresh exports contain only stub overlay crates, not the catalogue/codec implementation, so this fallback cannot be performed. Use a consumer-available check such as `bin/sotp catalog check`, with escalation for claims the CLI cannot verify.

This shipped convention still cites framework-only implementation paths at lines 39, 330, and 337–339. Exported `overlay/libs` contains only each crate's `Cargo.toml` and `src/lib.rs`, so these references are dead in every fresh consumer checkout; T021 would also copy them into the overlay. Replace them with the shipped schema reference and symbol-only descriptions.

The revised Related Documents entry preserves the obsolete `CompositePattern` symbol, but no such type exists in the current implementation or the shipped schema reference. The current kind model uses `TypeKindV2` with `StructKind`, `StructShape`, and `TypestateMarker`. Replace `CompositePattern` with the actual current symbols or describe the kind/shape contract generically.
必須の adapter/SSoT 同期監査と、修正後の参照・JSON・配布境界検証を実行中です。これは最終 verdict ではありません。

The IN-05 waiver reason relies on verification at “selection and result surfaces” and “the adapter,” contrary to the scope rule that waiver arguments must stand from the entry declaration and anchor text alone.

The AC-06 waiver reason relies on verification at “selection and result surfaces” and “the adapter,” contrary to the scope rule that waiver arguments must stand from the entry declaration and anchor text alone.
The AC-06 waiver reason for ConventionResolveService relies on properties being verified where other components produce them, rather than arguing solely from this entry’s declaration and the anchor.

The IN-07 waiver reason refers to the interactor’s preflight step and caller-controlled injection behavior; those external implementation facts are not valid evidence for a waiver that must stand from the declaration and anchor alone.
The AC-11 waiver reason relies on which control-flow branch calls the vocabulary and how that branch is verified, rather than arguing solely from CapabilityExecError’s declaration and AC-11.

The AC-07 waiver relies on the external claim “Which inputs produce which failure is decided by the implementation behind the port and is verified there.” That sentence is absent from both the `ConventionRequirementPort` declaration and AC-07, and refers to implementation/verification the waiver verifier does not receive. Rewrite the reason using only the declaration and anchor.

The `ConventionResolveError` waiver refers to external tests and producers through “where its own tests sit” and “the scan and the codec that produce these values, and are verified where they are decided.” Neither claim appears in the entry declaration or AC-07. Remove those external references and make the waiver argument solely from the permitted texts.

`ConventionResolveError` × AC-07 is recorded twice with mutually exclusive outcomes: a `voluntary_binding` at line 118 and this waiver. Waiver precedence suppresses voluntary-binding adjudication, so the six listed tests become dead evidence while remaining in the artifact. Keep only the outcome that represents the edge.

The AC-12 witness never supplies any competing `convention_refs`: its fake briefing is plain text and its project root is nonexistent. An implementation that additionally reads available track `convention_refs` would therefore remain green here while violating AC-12 in a real repository. Add and bind a trap case containing an unrelated track convention reference, assert that only resolver output is injected, and re-evaluate the verdict.

The delegate-in-host witness checks only that the discipline starts with the base text and retains the resolved path bullet. It would stay green if `CapabilityExecInteractor` post-processed the delegated discipline to omit the required instruction to read every listed document in full, violating IN-07/AC-10. Bind a test that compares the complete delegated discipline with the composed value, including the full-reading obligation.

`cli::ConventionsCommand.docs` repeats IN-06/AC-09’s whitespace rejection and no-registration behavior in prose. Per `no-upstream-restatement.md`, retain only the changed symbol/operation and rely on `spec_refs` for that contract.

`cli::ConventionsCommand::Resolve` orders its mirror fields as `capability, project_root`, while `cli_driver::ConventionResolveInput` and `usecase::ResolveConventionsQuery` use `project_root, capability`. No language-level constraint documents the divergence; align this command/input mirror chain.

The docs for `cli_driver::CapabilityNameArg`, `cli_driver::ConventionResolveDriver`, `cli_driver::ConventionResolveInput`, and `cli_driver::ConventionShippingCheckDriver` reproduce upstream validation, empty-result, fail-closed, rendering, and shipping-check behavior. Replace those paraphrases with concise symbol/operation descriptions plus the existing anchors, retaining only local adapter-design rationale.

The docs for `infrastructure::conventions_resolve::parse_convention_front_matter`, `infrastructure::conventions_resolve::scan_convention_requirements`, `infrastructure::template_conventions::list_convention_documents`, `infrastructure::CapabilityIdField`, and `infrastructure::ConventionFrontMatterDto` restate AC-07/AC-08/AC-18 failure and empty-state contracts. Reference those anchors instead of duplicating their behavior in catalogue prose.

The docs for `usecase::conventions_resolve::select_required_conventions`, `usecase::template_conventions::select_unsupplied_conventions`, `usecase::ConventionInventoryPort`, `usecase::ConventionRequirementPort`, and `usecase::ConventionResolveService` reproduce exact-match, ordering, empty-result, one-way comparison, failure, and no-write behavior from the spec. Reduce them to downstream type/operation descriptions and anchor references.

`usecase::ConventionInventoryPort::list_conventions` and `usecase::ConventionRequirementPort::scan_requirements` are synchronous contracts for filesystem tree walking and file reads, but neither entry acknowledges why blocking I/O is intentional. Declare the appropriate async color or document the deliberate synchronous CLI boundary.

The docs for `usecase::CapabilityExecError`, `usecase::CapabilityExecInteractor`, `usecase::CapabilityName`, and `usecase::DisciplineText` reproduce IN-06/IN-07, AC-09–AC-12, and CN-05 behavior such as execution ordering, both dispatch routes, and prohibition of re-resolution. Replace the duplicated contract with anchor citations while retaining type-local rationale.

The docs for `usecase::ConventionRequirement`, `usecase::ConventionResolution`, `usecase::ConventionResolveError`, `usecase::ConventionResolveInteractor`, `usecase::ConventionShippingCheckError`, `usecase::ConventionShippingVerdict`, and `usecase::ResolveConventionsQuery` restate AC-06–AC-09/AC-18 behavior, including complete failure lists and normal-empty states. Keep the structural/type rationale, but refer to the existing anchors for behavioral details.

`usecase::ConventionShippingCheckError::DocumentPathRejected.source` accepts the entire `ConventionResolveError`, admitting impossible states such as `FrontMatterUnparseable` or `DocumentUnreadable` even though the shipping inventory reads no contents and can only fail path validation here. Use a path-specific error or payload so those states are unrepresentable.

`usecase::conventions_resolve::ConventionCapabilityId` と `ConventionCapabilityIdError` の docs は、D4／IN-06／AC-07 の許容・拒否契約（padded 値の許容、empty／whitespace-only だけの拒否、fail-closed リストが exhaustive であるため条件を追加できない理由）を散文で再記述しています。`no-upstream-restatement.md` に従い、newtype・bridge・配置・error shape のローカルな型設計根拠だけを残し、上流の挙動と理由は既存の anchor 参照に委ねてください。

`usecase::conventions_resolve::ConventionCapabilityId` declares its constructor the single enforcement owner for AC-07’s blank-identifier condition, while `infrastructure::conventions_resolve::ConventionFrontMatterDto` also calls `into_requirement` the single enforcing site. The DTO only invokes the constructor and maps `ConventionCapabilityIdError` to the document-aware resolver error; describe it as the single mapping/conversion site so validation has exactly one declared owner.

`usecase::conventions_resolve::ConventionCapabilityId` は `try_new` を AC-07 の blank-identifier 条件の「single enforcing site」としていますが、`infrastructure::conventions_resolve::ConventionFrontMatterDto` も `into_requirement` を同じ条件の「single enforcing site」としています。単一の fail-closed rule に二つの owner が宣言されています。`try_new` を検証 owner、`into_requirement` を `ConventionResolveError::EmptyCapabilityId` への mapping／文書情報付加 site とするなど、責務を一意にしてください。

`usecase::ConventionDocumentPathError` restates the AC-06/AC-07 behavioral contract at length—canonical record shape, exact UTF-8/line-terminator rejection conditions, and their behavioral rationale—rather than referencing the upstream anchors. Keep the type-local variant, payload, ordering, and ownership rationale, but replace the upstream behavior explanation with anchor cites as required by `knowledge/conventions/no-upstream-restatement.md`.

`usecase::ConventionResolveError` restates AC-07's structural-anomaly category and its non-exhaustive semantics in the opening sentences. Because AC-07 owns that behavior contract, the catalogue should cite the anchor and retain only type-local information such as variant wiring and construction ownership.

`usecase::ConventionResolveError` claims “one variant per condition,” but AC-07 defines a non-exhaustive anomaly category, and the two current path-rejection conditions are intentionally composed under the single `DocumentPathRejected` variant. This both closes the upstream category and misstates the enum’s present shape. Replace it with an AC-07 anchor reference and retain only the type-local composition/ownership details, per `knowledge/conventions/no-upstream-restatement.md`.

`usecase::ConventionResolveError` now declares `ConventionRootUnlistable`, but its docs still classify only “the remaining three variants” and never name this variant's enforcement owner. The infrastructure directory scan both decides and constructs this failure; update the catalogue docs to record that single owner and remove the stale count.

`usecase::ConventionShippingCheckError` describes the structural fail-closed category as “one variant each” and later “all three variants,” turning the current enum membership into a closed behavioral enumeration. `usecase::ConventionShippingCheckError` still frames the structural fail-closed category as a closed one-to-one enumeration: “a variant apiece” is semantically identical to the previously rejected “one variant each.” This downstream completeness claim does not survive category growth and remains contrary to `knowledge/conventions/no-upstream-restatement.md`; use category-level wording and anchor references without asserting an exhaustive mapping.

`usecase::CapabilityExecInteractor` `docs` substantially restates upstream rationale and behavior (subdirectory scanning, AC-08 empty results, `CapabilityExecRequest` placement, `PathBuf` versus newtype, and mirror-chain consequences) instead of referring to upstream anchors. `serde_yaml::from_value` can fail before examining `required_for`. For example, valid YAML containing only `true: metadata` produces a boolean map key; deserializing that key as a struct field identifier fails, and this branch incorrectly reports `RequiredForNotStringArray`. This violates the promised unknown-key tolerance and AC-08’s requirement that an absent `required_for` succeed with the default value. Ensure unknown YAML keys are ignored regardless of their YAML scalar type, and reserve this error variant for failures in `required_for` itself.

`required_for` is deserialized directly into `Vec<CapabilityIdField>`, but `serde_yaml` coerces a YAML null/empty scalar to an empty sequence for `Vec`. Consequently, `required_for: null` or a bare `required_for:` succeeds as an empty declaration instead of returning `RequiredForNotStringArray`, violating AC-07’s fail-closed requirement for every non-string-array shape. Use a strict field deserializer that accepts only an actual YAML sequence and add null coverage.

The scan follows `*.md` file symlinks via `std::fs::read_to_string(entry.path())`, allowing a convention document path inside `knowledge/conventions` to load bytes from outside the trusted project tree. Reject symlinks with `symlink_metadata` before reading (and add an escape test).

`read_dir` follows symlinks in the convention-root path before any `DirEntry::file_type` check runs. If `knowledge` or `knowledge/conventions` is a directory symlink, out-of-tree files are scanned and reported under validated in-tree paths. Guard every component below `project_root` with no-follow metadata checks before listing it, and test root/ancestor symlinks.

After excluding directories and symlinks, every other `*.md` filesystem node is passed to `read_to_string`. A FIFO such as `blocked.md` can therefore block the resolver indefinitely. Require a regular file before reading, and fail closed or skip unsupported node types consistently.

`read_to_string` buffers an externally controlled convention document without a size limit. A sufficiently large or sparse file can exhaust process memory instead of producing a typed adapter error. Read through an explicit byte bound and fail closed when it is exceeded.

`sorted_entries` eagerly collects and sorts every directory entry. This both allocates without a bound—even for millions of non-Markdown entries—and establishes an observable infrastructure scan order that the briefing assigns to `ConventionResolution`; the order-sensitive scan tests entrench that ownership leak. Stream entries without imposing raw-result order, leaving canonical ordering to the usecase layer.

The directory symlink checks are TOCTOU snapshots. After the root guard or `entry.file_type()` accepts a directory, `read_dir` reopens its path and follows any symlink substituted in between, allowing an out-of-tree directory to be scanned under in-tree document identities. Traverse through atomic no-follow directory handles (or an equivalent fail-closed mechanism) rather than reopening checked paths.

The regular-file check is also separated from `File::open`. A concurrent replacement can turn the checked leaf into a symlink, FIFO, or device; `File::open` then follows it or blocks before the byte limit can help. Use an atomic no-follow/nonblocking open and validate the opened handle's file type, following the existing waiver-cache/output-collector pattern.

The new limits are only per file and per directory. Recursive traversal still has no aggregate document, byte, entry, or depth budget, while `requirements` retains every decoded requirement. A tree with up to 10,000 children at each level can therefore drive unbounded I/O and memory growth without violating either local limit. Carry a total scan budget through recursion and fail closed when exhausted.

`sorted_entries` still imposes an observable deterministic order on the raw adapter result, and the scan tests assert that order. This keeps ordering policy in infrastructure even though the briefing assigns ordering and deduplication exclusively to `ConventionResolution::from_matches`. Iterate without defining raw-result order and leave canonical ordering to the usecase-owned constructor.

`sorted_entries` sorts every directory before scanning, so the infrastructure adapter establishes a deterministic traversal/output order. The briefing assigns ordering exclusively to `ConventionResolution::from_matches`, while the scan tests further expose this adapter order as contractual through exact vector assertions. Remove the adapter-side sort and make scan assertions order-independent so ordering remains owned by the use-case layer.

`scan_entries` constructs a `ConventionDocumentPath` before checking an entry's type or `.md` extension. On Unix, an otherwise ignored neighbor such as `knowledge/conventions/notes\n.txt` is a valid directory entry but is rejected as `NotRenderableAsRecord`, so it aborts the entire scan with `DocumentPathRejected` instead of being ignored. A similarly named `.md` file also disproves the comments and tests claiming no real tree can reach this lift, leaving that error path uncovered. Filter non-document entries before path validation and add real-tree coverage for both cases.

`front_matter.is_null()` treats explicit YAML null documents (`null`, `~`, or `Null`) the same as a genuinely empty front-matter block. Those values are non-mapping front matter, but the codec returns the default DTO instead of failing closed as `FrontMatterUnparseable`, silently treating malformed metadata as no declarations. Detect an actually empty block before parsing, reject explicit null values, and add coverage for the null spellings.

The prior path-validation fix remains incomplete for directories: `document_path(candidate)?` runs before determining whether a directory contains any Markdown documents. A tree containing only `knowledge/conventions/two\nlines/README.txt` therefore fails with `DocumentPathRejected` even though the subtree has no `**/*.md` candidate and should be ignored. Carry the raw relative directory path during traversal and validate the complete path only when an actual Markdown document is found; an `.md` below such a directory will still fail closed correctly.

`declares_nothing` applies Rust's Unicode `trim()` before deciding whether a line is a YAML comment. For example, a front-matter line beginning with U+00A0 followed by `#not-a-comment` is a non-mapping YAML scalar because NBSP is not YAML separation whitespace, but `trim()` removes it and this helper treats the line as comment-only, returning an empty DTO without parsing. This leaves a fail-open path for invalid/non-mapping front matter. Use YAML's lexical rules (or parser tokens) for the empty/comment-only distinction and add coverage for non-YAML Unicode whitespace.

`parse_convention_front_matter` delegates block detection to a reader that recognizes only an exact `---\n` opener. A valid document using CRLF starts with `---\r\n`, so the reader returns `None` and this function silently returns the default DTO, discarding every `required_for` declaration. This is a fail-open codec path for ordinary Windows-style files. Accept CRLF delimiters and add an end-to-end test whose entire front-matter block uses CRLF.

`declares_nothing` uses `str::lines()`, which does not split on a bare carriage return even though YAML treats `` as a line break. Consequently, `---
# noterequired_for: [implementer]
---
` is valid mapping front matter, but the entire first Rust line starts with `#`, so the function returns `true` and silently discards the declaration. Split on every YAML line-break form or use parser-level token information when distinguishing an empty/comment-only block.

The shared delimiter reader still recognizes only LF/CRLF and requires `---` at byte zero, although the YAML reader accepts a leading UTF-8 BOM and additional line breaks such as a lone CR. Consequently, both `\u{FEFF}---
required_for: [implementer]
---
` and `---required_for: [implementer]---` are classified as having no block, so the convention codec silently returns its default and drops the declaration. Normalize an optional BOM and use the parser-compatible line-break set consistently for opening, scanning, closing, and trimming delimiters.

The `declares_nothing` fast path returns before YAML validation, so malformed front matter can silently become an empty requirement. For example, a block containing `\t# comment` or a comment containing U+0001 satisfies this predicate, although libyaml rejects tab indentation/control characters. The document then loses its `required_for` enforcement instead of producing `FrontMatterUnparseable`. Validate even lexically empty/comment-only blocks before returning the default DTO.

`let Ok(true) = ... else` treats every symlink-guard error as an empty convention tree. For example, if `knowledge` is a regular file or cannot be traversed, the guard returns `NotADirectory` or `PermissionDenied`, and this function returns `Ok(Vec::new())` without reaching `ConventionRootUnlistable`. This silently converts an unreadable/malformed tree into “no requirements,” violating AC-07’s fail-closed contract. Distinguish an absent or deliberately skipped symlinked root from inspection errors, and add regression coverage for the latter.

`InvalidInput` is not a symlink-specific signal: the guard also forwards filesystem inspection errors with their original kind, and filesystem operations return `InvalidInput` for malformed paths such as an interior-NUL `project_root`. This arm therefore converts some invalid roots into `Ok(Vec::new())` instead of failing closed with `ConventionRootUnlistable`. Distinguish explicit symlink rejection structurally and propagate other `InvalidInput` failures.

The added regression test does not exercise the new guard-error arm: making `knowledge/conventions` a file causes the guard to return `Ok(true)`, with `bounded_entries` producing the error afterward. Add a case where `knowledge` itself is a file (or otherwise untraversable), which makes the guard return `Err(NotADirectory)`, and assert `ConventionRootUnlistable`; otherwise the originally affected branch can regress without failing this test.

`is_symlink_rejection` identifies the error’s origin by searching its rendered message. Inspection failures generated above include the inspected path in that message, so a non-symlink `InvalidInput` path containing this marker—for example a programmatic `project_root` containing `"refusing to follow symlink\0"`—is misclassified as a refused link. The scanner then returns an ordinary empty result instead of `ConventionRootUnlistable`, violating fail-closed behavior. Use a typed inner error/sentinel that can be downcast rather than message matching, and test a non-symlink `InvalidInput` error carrying marker-like text.

The new typed discriminator is the only protection against treating a non-symlink `InvalidInput` inspection failure as an empty tree, but no test exercises that distinction. Existing guard tests only assert that symlinks return some error, while the scanner’s non-symlink case produces `NotADirectory`, not the same-kind failure that caused the bug. Add true/false tests for `is_symlink_rejection`, including a plain `InvalidInput` error whose message resembles the old marker, or an equivalent public scanner regression.

`rustix::fs::DirEntry::file_type()` can return `FileType::Unknown` when the filesystem supplies `DT_UNKNOWN`. This sets all three classification flags to false, so `scan_entries` silently skips valid Markdown files and entire subdirectories as non-regular nodes. The adapter can consequently return a successful empty/incomplete resolution instead of the AC-06 contents or an AC-07 fail-closed error. Resolve unknown types with a handle-relative, no-follow metadata lookup (or return an error) before classifying the entry.

The initial convention-root open remains vulnerable to an ancestor-symlink TOCTOU. After `reject_symlinks_below` checks `knowledge`, that directory can be replaced by a symlink before `open_directory(&convention_root)`. `O_NOFOLLOW` protects only the trailing `conventions` component, so the open can follow the substituted `knowledge` into another tree; if that link is dangling, `ENOENT` is incorrectly converted to an empty result. Open `project_root` as the trusted anchor and descend through both components with handle-relative `openat(..., O_NOFOLLOW)`, failing closed on any link. The handle-relative traversal below the root does not protect this first pathname open.

`open_convention_root` erases which open produced `NotFound`, so a nonexistent or dangling caller-supplied `project_root` is returned as a successful empty convention set. No repository was opened in that case; it is not the legitimate “repository exists but has no convention directory” state. Since `--project-root` is accepted directly, a typo can silently bypass the AC-07 fail-closed path. Open the trusted anchor separately and map its failures to `ConventionRootUnlistable`; only `NotFound` while descending to `knowledge` or `conventions` should return empty.

After `open_convention_root` has returned a directory handle, `NotFound` from `bounded_entries` means listing that opened root failed (for example, `getdents` can report `ENOENT` after concurrent removal); it is no longer evidence that the convention root was absent. Returning an empty result here again conflates “not inspected” with “contains no documents.” Map every `bounded_entries` error to `ConventionRootUnlistable`.

The whole-scan budget is charged too late. `bounded_entries` fully reads, classifies, and stores a child directory before recursive `scan_entries` decrements `remaining_entries`. A depth-64 chain with roughly 10,000 entries per level can therefore enumerate and retain about 640,000 entries while spending only one budget unit per descended directory, bypassing the advertised 20,000-entry traversal bound. Charge the shared budget as entries are produced, including the root listing.

`requires()` compares `CapabilityName` values, but `CapabilityName::try_new` stores a trimmed `NonEmptyString`. Consequently, `required_for: [" reviewer "]` matches a query for `reviewer`, violating IN-06/AC-06’s non-empty, exact-string matching contract. Preserve non-blank identifiers without normalization (and cover whitespace near-misses).

`with_conventions` unconditionally adds the `## Project conventions` section heading, contrary to CN-06's requirement that rendered convention obligations contain no section heading. This makes both dispatch routes carry non-conforming discipline text.

`try_new` now rejects paths that remain inside `knowledge/conventions/` when they contain CR/LF or non-UTF-8 bytes. This adds a fail-closed case beyond AC-07/D4, which explicitly limits resolver failure to five conditions and only rejects a path for escaping the convention root. Either preserve such paths losslessly in output or obtain an upstream contract change before rejecting them.

The cross-dispatch test does not fully pin the per-dispatch contract. It always returns the same document, never inspects `dispatches`, and changes capability on the second call. Thus a per-capability cache could skip resolution on a repeated same-capability dispatch, or the interactor could resolve the second capability but reuse the first composed discipline, while every assertion still passes. Add a same-capability repeat plus capability-specific resolver results, and assert the second dispatched discipline uses only its own resolution.

AC-17 requires old-path references in every existing ADR/research note to remain unchanged, but D10 and OUT-05 exempt only historical notes that are not referenced as current procedure. As written, a live ADR/research note cannot satisfy both IN-10/AC-16's live-reference cleanup and AC-17's blanket no-change requirement. Restore the missing 「現行手順として参照されていない」 qualifier.

A zero-match resolution produces `stdout: Some("")`, but this path passes it to `driver_outcome_to_exit`, whose `println!` emits a spurious blank line. Thus the normal empty result contains one empty stdout line instead of zero path lines, violating AC-06/AC-08. Represent empty stdout as absent before emission and add a dispatch-level empty-result assertion.

The new public `Resolve` dispatch has no error-path test. All dispatch tests use readable convention trees, so resolver failures are not verified to return `ExitCode::FAILURE` without partial stdout, despite the required public-API error coverage and the briefing's error-propagation check.

D4 embeds an operational resolver command, output contract, and exhaustive fail-closed validation behavior. This obscures the architectural decision; delegate these implementation/schema details to the capability or harness contract and retain only the ownership/discovery decision.

D6 specifies dispatcher entrypoint mechanics, outcome-specific payload wiring, host/provider delegation behavior, and prohibited alternate paths. This is workflow/capability contract detail that obscures the decision and should be delegated to the relevant SSoT.

D10 prescribes template smoke checks, dead-reference detection exclusions, historical-path exemptions, and review-based enforcement. These are operational gate and workflow rules rather than the architectural decision, so they should be removed or delegated to the relevant harness/review SSoT.

D1 mandates one directory-level `overlay` classification and explicitly rejects `exclude` because it cannot supply overlay content, but its closing summary says the replacement is directory `exclude` + overlay. These instructions are incompatible and could cause the initial conventions to be omitted. Change the summary to directory `overlay` or otherwise align it with the preceding decision.
findings.category: inconsistent decisions within the same ADR

findings.message: The Negative consequence still embeds the dispatcher outcome identifiers `executed` and `delegate-in-host` in an operational conformance-test prescription. This is precisely the mechanism detail the accepted repair delegates away and it obscures the provider-neutral D6 decision. Retain the requirement for both external execution and in-host delegation, but remove the concrete outcome names and test-wiring terminology.

`ConventionDocumentPath` accepts arbitrary paths beneath the convention root, including filenames containing newlines and, on Unix, non-UTF-8 bytes. Converting each path with `Display` and joining on `\n` is therefore not a lossless one-record-per-line encoding: one matched file can produce multiple apparent records, while distinct non-UTF-8 paths can collapse to the same replacement-character text. This breaks the canonical machine-readable result promised by IN-05/AC-06. Enforce a render-safe path invariant or use an unambiguous encoding, with boundary-value coverage.

The IN-05/AC-06 binding for this test attributes exact-match selection and stable ordering to `ConventionsCompositionRoot`: the fixture excludes the nonmatching document and the exact stdout assertion fixes the returned order. This root only establishes the adapter → interactor → driver graph; matching is established downstream and deduplication/order are inherited from `ConventionResolution`. Keep the composition binding limited to evidence of the selected object graph and bind those behavioral guarantees to their owning entries.

`CapabilityExecInteractor::new` still has a second construction site in the infrastructure test, but it supplies only three arguments and omits the newly required convention resolver and project root. This causes test compilation to fail and leaves construction outside the composition root inconsistent with the new wiring contract.
